title: Array-Backed Directed Relational Graph Exploratory Simulation
purpose: Test whether U_Omega can generate persistent asymmetric triadic closures from random distinction-array noise.

not_allowed: treating grid position as physical space

formal_targets.root_schema: U_Omega := [chi_D -> E -> delta_a -> Arb_A -> Delta -> chi_D']
formal_targets.array_reading: Persistent oriented relation pattern over chi_D

orientation_array.entry_meaning: orientation condition affecting admissibility and selection

floor_rule.note: exclusion is boundary-generation, not automatically total 0-state

zero_state_rule.if: global E(chi_D) == 0 or admissible Q is empty everywhere

primary_metrics.relation_survival_rate: fraction of chi_D entries remaining above epsilon
primary_metrics.TC_asym_count: number of stable directed asymmetric triadic closures
primary_metrics.TC_asym_lifetime_mean: mean persistence duration of detected closures
primary_metrics.orientation_coherence: consistency of orientation pattern inside closure candidates
primary_metrics.residue_support: degree to which prior persistence predicts future relation survival
primary_metrics.topology_preservation: stability of directed connectivity under perturbation

M0_full.description: Full U_Omega-inspired update with distinction, admissibility, arbitration, orientation, and residue.

M2_no_residue.description: Disable R inscription and history-conditioned admissibility.

M3_no_orientation.description: Remove orientation/tuning array from admissibility and selection.

M4_no_floor.description: Remove epsilon floor and allow distinction to drift to zero.

M5_static_admissibility.description: Freeze admissibility mask so topology cannot evolve through residue.

M6_memoryless_noise.description: Random update process with matched value distribution but no U_Omega chain.

FA_SIM_001.name: Zero-distinction continuation attack
FA_SIM_001.failure_condition: system continues lawful updates when E_global == 0

FA_SIM_002.name: Random-equivalence attack
FA_SIM_002.failure_condition: M1 or M6 matches M0 on TC_asym persistence within tolerance

FA_SIM_003.name: Residue-irrelevance attack
FA_SIM_003.failure_condition: M2 performs equal or better than M0 on closure lifetime

FA_SIM_004.name: Orientation-decorative attack
FA_SIM_004.failure_condition: M3 shows no measurable change in closure class selection

FA_SIM_005.name: Floor-irrelevance attack
FA_SIM_005.failure_condition: M4 avoids collapse/freeze as well as M0

FA_SIM_006.name: Projection-aliasing attack
FA_SIM_006.failure_condition: same final visual topology is treated as same process history

governance_notes: Graphs are interpretive projections of chi_D, not primitive substrates.
Arrays are not state containers; they are relation-addressing organizations.
Nodes are addressable participation sites, not objects.
Stable triangles count only as TC_asym candidates until persistence and ablation tests pass.
Failure is informative: collapse, freeze, and disconnection are first-class outcomes.
